capabilities.missingDependency: an accepted executable route issuing a mandate-scoped representative session
capabilities.reason: API-02 C13 accepts identity-side issuance operations, but none of them issues or validates a session bound to an elected mandate. No accepted route exists that a WS-04 browser could call to become authenticated as a mandate holder.
capabilities.frontendBehaviour: The workspace starts in the anonymous state, states that mandate sessions cannot be established against any accepted runtime, and offers no credential entry that would imply otherwise.

capabilities.missingDependency: an accepted mandate register exposing the mandate, its level, and its active authority window
capabilities.reason: The only mandate register source in the programme is office-mandate-service, which exists solely inside the unaccepted PACK-20 candidate archive. compliance-service.RepresentationMandate is legal power of attorney under PACK-09 and is not an elected mandate.
capabilities.frontendBehaviour: Scope is never resolved from the network. Every protected surface refuses with scope_mismatch or unavailable and names the missing register.

capabilities.missingDependency: an accepted server-side authority check evaluated at commit time
capabilities.reason: Commit-time revalidation is a server obligation. With no accepted mandate service there is nothing to revalidate against, and the client is forbidden from deciding authority itself.
capabilities.frontendBehaviour: No action that would require commit-time revalidation is offered as executable. The requirement is displayed, not simulated.

capabilities.missingDependency: an accepted executable step-up ceremony returning a raised assurance level
capabilities.reason: Assurance levels are declared in the accepted policy records, but no accepted route performs a step-up ceremony.
capabilities.frontendBehaviour: Surfaces that require step-up render the step_up_required state with the reason, and the trigger is inert by construction rather than disabled by styling.

capabilities.missingDependency: an accepted executable route listing mandate-scoped citizen cases
capabilities.reason: The desk service exists only inside the unaccepted PACK-29 candidate archive, and FIR-REP-001 is recorded as captured, not accepted.
capabilities.frontendBehaviour: The desk renders the unavailable state with the named dependency. No placeholder case list is shown, because a fabricated list is indistinguishable from a real one to the user.

capabilities.missingDependency: an accepted executable route returning a single case within mandate scope
capabilities.reason: Same dependency as the intake list. Case content is confidential and is the data class this workspace is most constrained around.
capabilities.frontendBehaviour: Detail routes refuse non-disclosingly: the refusal is identical whether the case does not exist or lies outside scope.

capabilities.missingDependency: an accepted executable case assignment operation
capabilities.reason: Assignment mutates server-held state; no accepted route accepts such a mutation.
capabilities.frontendBehaviour: The action is described in the action register with its authority requirement and reported as blocked. It is never offered as executable.

capabilities.missingDependency: an accepted executable state-transition operation with optimistic-concurrency semantics
capabilities.reason: Case state transitions are server-authoritative and require a version precondition. Neither the operation nor the version token has an accepted definition.
capabilities.frontendBehaviour: Transitions are not attempted. The state machine models the safe outcomes, including the uncertain outcome, and is exercised only under the governed test profile.

capabilities.missingDependency: an accepted executable route recording an outbound response against a case
capabilities.reason: No accepted route accepts case correspondence.
capabilities.frontendBehaviour: Composition surfaces are not presented as a send path. Nothing composed is described as delivered.

capabilities.missingDependency: an accepted executable search operation that is server-side scope-bound
capabilities.reason: Search must be constrained on the server. A client-side filter over a client-held corpus is not a scoped search, and a cross-mandate search is prohibited outright.
capabilities.frontendBehaviour: Search is unavailable. The interface never offers an unscoped search field, so there is no surface on which a cross-mandate query could be typed.

capabilities.missingDependency: an accepted executable route returning stored position drafts
capabilities.reason: No accepted route stores or returns position drafts.
capabilities.frontendBehaviour: The position surface renders unavailable rather than an empty list, because an empty list asserts that nothing exists.

capabilities.missingDependency: an accepted executable route persisting a draft
capabilities.reason: No accepted route persists a draft.
capabilities.frontendBehaviour: A draft composed in this workspace exists only in volatile memory for the life of the surface. It is labelled as unsaved, and no browser storage receives it.

capabilities.missingDependency: an accepted executable route accepting an internal submission
capabilities.reason: No accepted route accepts a submission.
capabilities.frontendBehaviour: Submission is reported blocked with the named dependency. The workspace never reports a draft as submitted.

capabilities.missingDependency: an accepted executable route returning deviation records with provenance
capabilities.reason: transparency-service publishes finished items; it holds no deviation record model, and the desk service that would hold one is unaccepted.
capabilities.frontendBehaviour: Unavailable state with the named dependency.

capabilities.missingDependency: an accepted executable route recording a deviation against a governed decision
capabilities.reason: No accepted route accepts a deviation record.
capabilities.frontendBehaviour: The composition surface exists and enforces the record's shape locally, including the requirement that a deviation references a decision and cannot alter it. Nothing is transmitted.

capabilities.missingDependency: an accepted executable route resolving a governed decision identifier to its published record
capabilities.reason: A deviation must reference a real decision. No accepted route resolves decision identifiers.
capabilities.frontendBehaviour: References are accepted as opaque text and explicitly marked unverified. The workspace does not claim a reference is valid.

capabilities.missingDependency: an accepted executable route returning a representative's own declarations
capabilities.reason: compliance-service models declarations at specification level only; no accepted executable route exists, and its RepresentationMandate is legal power of attorney rather than an elected mandate.
capabilities.frontendBehaviour: Unavailable state with the named dependency.

capabilities.missingDependency: an accepted executable route accepting a declaration submission
capabilities.reason: No accepted route accepts a declaration.
capabilities.frontendBehaviour: The form validates locally and reports the submission blocked. It never reports acceptance, and it never asserts a compliance obligation has been met.

capabilities.missingDependency: a server-authoritative proposal and authorization contract: a proposal state distinct from PUBLISHED, and an authorization decided by the server rather than asserted by the caller
capabilities.reason: transparency-service has a single publication state, PUBLISHED, and it authorises by a caller-supplied actor_is_authorized boolean. There is no proposal state to submit into, and the authorization gate is not an authorization gate.
capabilities.frontendBehaviour: The workspace offers proposal composition only, states in the interface that a proposal is not an approval, and reports submission blocked. It never sets, sends or relies on an authorization flag of its own.
capabilities.securityFinding: A caller-supplied actor_is_authorized boolean is a self-asserted authorization: the caller declares its own permission and the service accepts the declaration. FRONT-05 must not treat it as evidence that any authorization occurred, and must not build a privileged path on it â doing so would let a proposal reach publication carrying nothing but the proposer's own claim of being allowed to publish. This is a defect in the dependency, not a gap in it: the capability stays blocked until a server-authoritative authorization contract exists, and would remain blocked even if a proposal route were added while the boolean stayed.

capabilities.missingDependency: a route returning a publication state whose approval was decided by an authority other than the proposer
capabilities.reason: No accepted executable transparency route ships, and the model behind it records no deciding authority â publication is authorised by the caller's own actor_is_authorized boolean.
capabilities.frontendBehaviour: Publication state is shown as unknown rather than assumed, and an approved state is presented as public only when a deciding authority and a public rendition reference are both present.
capabilities.securityFinding: An observed publication state carries no independent evidence of who approved it, because the service records no deciding authority. A state read back from such a service cannot distinguish an approval by the publication authority from one the proposer asserted about itself, so this workspace treats an approved state with no recorded decider as not public â see mayPresentAsPublic in domain/publication.ts.

capabilities.missingDependency: an accepted executable route returning active conflict restrictions for a mandate
capabilities.reason: No accepted route returns restrictions.
capabilities.frontendBehaviour: Restrictions cannot be read, so the workspace fails closed: it neither asserts that a restriction is absent nor treats an unknown restriction as cleared.

capabilities.missingDependency: not applicable â the capability is prohibited for this workspace, not merely blocked
capabilities.reason: A subject may never clear a restriction over themselves. This is a prohibition, so it would remain unsupported even if an accepted route existed.
capabilities.frontendBehaviour: No surface, no action descriptor, and no port exists. The prohibition is enforced by absence and asserted by a total function returning false.

capabilities.missingDependency: an accepted executable read route over a protected register
capabilities.reason: WS-04 holds no registry custody and may only reference registry data by reading it. No accepted read route exists.
capabilities.frontendBehaviour: Registry-derived facts are shown as unavailable. No registry mutation surface exists at all.

capabilities.missingDependency: an accepted executable route returning a decided eligibility status
capabilities.reason: WS-04 may display an eligibility decision made elsewhere but may never make one. No accepted route supplies a decision to display.
capabilities.frontendBehaviour: Eligibility is displayed as undetermined-elsewhere, with the explicit statement that this workspace does not decide it.

capabilities.missingDependency: any control-plane implementation whatsoever
capabilities.reason: CTRL is recorded NOT_STARTED and no code is on disk. There is no audit surface to read.
capabilities.frontendBehaviour: The workspace states that its own actions are not currently audited by an accepted control plane, which is a limitation the operator must know.

capabilities.missingDependency: a connected accepted telemetry platform
capabilities.reason: No telemetry platform is connected. The allowlist and the content prohibitions are implemented and tested regardless, so that the constraint is already binding when a platform arrives.
capabilities.frontendBehaviour: No telemetry leaves the browser. The validator asserts the allowlist is enforced and that case content can never enter an event.

capabilities.reason: Rendering a safe refusal is performed entirely by this workspace and depends on nothing external.
capabilities.frontendBehaviour: Every refusal kind renders a safe message, a committed/not-committed/unknown statement, and one safe next action, with non-disclosure preserved where required.

capabilities.reason: Binding every route and action to exactly one mandate scope, and rejecting any request that carries none or more than one, is local structure. It is presentation-side only and never a substitute for the server decision.
capabilities.frontendBehaviour: There is no representation of an unbounded scope in the type system, so a cross-mandate request has no expressible form.

capabilities.reason: Directing the user to the governed non-digital path when a digital path is blocked is local and always available.
capabilities.frontendBehaviour: Each blocked surface names the offline route that remains valid, so no citizen matter is dropped because the software is unfinished.
